newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees HUF70-80bln surplus from 97 sell-offs.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees HUF70-80bln surplus from 97 sell-offs.

text.p: Hungary's government budget revenues from privatisation may exceed the 50 billion forint target for 1997 by 70 to 80 billion, the state privatisation agency APV told the daily Vilaggazdasag on Monday.

APV chairman Arpad Kovacs said the 70 to 80 billion forint surplus will flow in the government budget if APV can sell in 1997 stakes in OTP, the country's largest commercial bank, and national telephone company Matav.
The parliament amended the privatisation law two weeks ago to allow the state-owned stake in Matav and OTP to be reduced to one special rights share from 25 percent plus one share.
Originally, APV was expected to generate revenues of 180 billion forints and pay 50 billion to the government budget.
Prime Minister Gyula Horn confirmed earlier this month that surplus privatisation revenues would be spent on reducing the state debt.
The 70 to 80 billion forint surplus will enable Hungary to cut interest expenditures by 12 to 15 billion forints, the paper said.
